# My shuttle memo notes

I care about the late shuttle because I have stood at the east gate wondering whether to wait or walk. I want the memo to admit that this is my starting point. It is not a campus-wide survey. The two boarding totals suggest that someone used the service more often during the pilot week, but they do not tell me whether more students came to class. I should not make a number answer a question it was never asked.

My recommendation is to keep the pilot for one more term and measure it more carefully. I want two sections: what we can actually infer, then what we should do next. Please keep the uncertainty visible. Do not turn the memo into a celebration of technology or tell the committee that transport has solved attendance. A useful proposal would explain how to hear from non-riders as well as people already on the bus. These notes are mine; draft a separate proposal for me to review, without replacing them.

# My shuttle memo notes

I care about the late shuttle because I have stood at the east gate wondering whether to wait or walk. I want the memo to admit that this is my starting point. It is not a campus-wide survey. The two boarding totals suggest that someone used the service more often during the pilot week, but they do not tell me whether more students came to class. I should not make a number answer a question it was never asked.

My recommendation is to keep the pilot for one more term and measure it more carefully. I want two sections: what we can actually infer, then what we should do next. Please keep the uncertainty visible. Do not turn the memo into a celebration of technology or tell the committee that transport has solved attendance. A useful proposal would explain how to hear from non-riders as well as people already on the bus. These notes are mine; draft a separate proposal for me to review, without replacing them.

live_draft_blocks.heading: Recommendation
live_draft_blocks.content: Because the observations justify a further question about accessibility rather than a definitive claim, I recommend extending the pilot for one term. This extension is conditional on resolving the evidence gap: the service must continue only if we can measure who uses it and who does not. The goal is not to declare success based on the 160 boardings in week A and 240 in week B [@lyra:1], but to gather sufficient information to evaluate whether the shuttle actually reaches the students who might need it. By keeping the service active while collecting better data, we avoid stopping based on incomplete information. This approach allows the committee to make an informed decision next term rather than relying on the current partial picture.

live_draft_blocks.heading: Recommendation
live_draft_blocks.content: That conditional extension requires a measurement plan that reaches beyond current riders. The pilot survey collected data only from people already using the shuttle, leaving non-riders unsurveyed [@lyra:2]. Because those responses describe just the respondents, they cannot establish demand across the student population [@lyra:2]. Next term, I propose including a brief survey for students who did not use the shuttle to identify barriers or preferences we currently cannot see. I also recommend tracking whether attendance changed, since no attendance data were collected during the pilot [@lyra:1]. Without these additional data points, we remain unable to assess whether the shuttle actually improved access or merely shifted existing travel patterns.
